title: The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle
text:
The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle posits that there are inherent limits to the precision with which certain pairs of physical properties, such as a particle's position and its momentum, can be simultaneously known. Measuring one property necessarily disturbs the system in a way that prevents equally precise knowledge of the paired complementary variable.

This limitation is not attributed to instrumental error or technical deficiency, but rather represents a fundamental constraint built into the framework of quantum mechanics itself. It fundamentally challenges classical Newtonian notions of determinism by suggesting that perfect predictive knowledge about physical systems at the subatomic level is mathematically impossible.
